#this chunk of code filters through all the nos and separates them into nos with discourse and nos with 
#sentential, so that they eventually get their own graph
```{r split_no}
nos_labels <- read_csv("processed_data/all_nos_labeled.csv",
                       col_select = c(token_id, label)) %>%
  transmute(
    id = as.numeric(token_id),
    no_type = case_when(
      label == "D" ~ "no_discourse",
      label == "S" ~ "no_sentential",
      TRUE         ~ "no_unclassified"
    )
  )

Spanish_tokens <- Spanish_tokens %>%
  select(-any_of("no_type")) %>%
  left_join(nos_labels, by = "id") %>%
  mutate(logical_word = case_when(
    !is.na(no_type)      ~ no_type,
    logical_word == "no" ~ "no_unclassified",
    TRUE                 ~ logical_word
  ))
Spanish_tokens %>% filter(str_starts(logical_word, "no_")) %>% count(logical_word)
```


this chunk of code creates another data frame that calculates the cumalative relative frequency of each of the words in the logical words and sorts them by speaker age
# stan is not comiling so forcing data may be a problem...
these function words include: 
```{r}
functionword_relfreq <-
  
  child_data <- Spanish_tokens %>%
  filter(speaker == "child") %>%
  mutate(target_child_age = floor(target_child_age)) %>%  # only change
  group_by(logical_word, target_child_age, speaker) %>%
  summarise(freq = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(freq = as.numeric(freq)) %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    logical_word,
    speaker,
    target_child_age = 0:10,
    
    fill = list(freq = 0)
  ) %>%
  mutate(freq = ifelse(target_child_age <= 10, 0, freq))


parent_data <- Spanish_tokens %>%
  filter(speaker != "child") %>%
  mutate(target_child_age = floor(target_child_age)) %>%  # only change
  group_by(logical_word, target_child_age, speaker) %>%
  summarise(freq = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(freq = as.numeric(freq))

functionword_relfreq <- bind_rows(child_data, parent_data) %>%
  group_by(speaker, target_child_age) %>%
  mutate(
    total = sum(freq),
    relfreq = ifelse(total == 0, 0, freq / total),
    ppt = relfreq * 1000
  ) %>%
  group_by(logical_word, speaker) %>%
  arrange(target_child_age) %>%
  mutate(
    cum_freq = cumsum(freq),
    cum_total = cumsum(total),
    cumulative_relfreq = ifelse(cum_total == 0, 1e-6, cum_freq / cum_total),
    cumulative_ppt = cumulative_relfreq * 1000
  )

  saveRDS(functionword_relfreq, "functionword_relfreq.RDS")

```

# new separated -- this shows the two separate sentential versus discourse plots --> this is the new growth fitting curve that separates the sentential versus discourse no 
```{r Neg_No_Growth_Model_split, include=FALSE}
fit_no <- function(which_no, fit_file) {
  brm(
    bf(
      cumulative_ppt ~ upperAsymptote * exp(
        -exp(((growthRate * exp(1)) / upperAsymptote) * (lag - target_child_age) + 1)
      ),
      upperAsymptote ~ 1,
      growthRate ~ 1,
      lag ~ 1,
      nl = TRUE
    ),
    data = filter(functionword_relfreq,
                  logical_word == which_no,
                  speaker == "child"),
    prior = c(
      prior(uniform(0, 80), nlpar = "upperAsymptote", lb = 0, ub = 80),
      prior(uniform(0, 10), nlpar = "growthRate", lb = 0, ub = 10),
      prior(uniform(10, 72), nlpar = "lag", lb = 10, ub = 72)
    ),
    iter = 10000,
    file = fit_file
  )
}

neg_no_sentential_model <- fit_no("no_sentential", "spanish_neg_no_sentential_fit")
neg_no_discourse_model  <- fit_no("no_discourse",  "spanish_neg_no_discourse_fit")
```

#new labels 
#This chunk pulls the estimated onset age (“lag”) out of each fitted growth model, puts the two estimates in one table, and saves the table

```{r age_of_production_split}
get_lag <- function(model, label) {
  summ <- fixef(model)
  data.frame(
    logical_word = label,
    Estimate  = round(summ["lag_Intercept", "Estimate"], 1),
    Est.Error = round(summ["lag_Intercept", "Est.Error"], 1),
    Q2.5      = round(summ["lag_Intercept", "Q2.5"], 1),
    Q97.5     = round(summ["lag_Intercept", "Q97.5"], 1)
  )
}

age_of_production_no_split <- bind_rows(
  get_lag(neg_no_sentential_model, "no_sentential"),
  get_lag(neg_no_discourse_model,  "no_discourse")
)

saveRDS(age_of_production_no_split, "../processed_data/age_of_production_no_split.RDS")
```

This plot of code creates graphs for the function word no for children vs children, where the first 10 months are zeroed out 
This code plots developmental trajectories for the Spanish negation marker **no** across child and caregiver speech.

To ground the model, ages 1–10 months are assigned cumulative frequencies of zero. Maternal and paternal speech are also merged into a single **Parent** speaker category.

The word **no** functions as a negation marker in Spanish.

Example:

> *No quiero leche.*  
> “I do not want milk.”

```{r negation_no}
functionword_relfreq %>%
  filter(logical_word %in% c("no_sentential", "no_discourse")) %>%
  #filter(target_child_age > 10) %>%
  # mutate(speaker_role = ifelse(speaker_role %in% c("Mother", "Father"),
  #                              "Parent",
  #                              speaker_role)) %>%

  ggplot(aes(target_child_age, cumulative_ppt, color = logical_word)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(.~speaker) +
  theme_bw() + 
  xlab("Age (Months)") + ylab("Cumulative Parts Per Thousand")


```

##### Si (Done)

This code plots developmental trajectories for the Spanish affirmation marker **sí** across child and caregiver speech. The first 10 months are zeroed out to ground the model. In this context, **sí** is the Spanish equivalent of “yes.”

Example:

> *Sí, quiero más.*  
> “Yes, I want more.”


```{r negation_si}
functionword_relfreq %>%
  filter(logical_word=="si") %>%
  ggplot(aes(target_child_age, cumulative_ppt)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(.~speaker) +
  theme_bw() +
  xlab("Age (Months)") + ylab("Cumulative Parts Per Thousand")
```
this allows us to see max amounts to set the priors 
```{r}
functionword_relfreq %>%
  filter(logical_word == "si", speaker == "child") %>%
  summarise(max_ppt = max(cumulative_ppt, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_age = max(target_child_age, na.rm = TRUE))
```

### Bayesian Growth Curve Model

This chunk fits a Bayesian Gompertz growth curve to the developmental trajectory of the Spanish affirmation marker **sí** (“yes”) in child speech.

The model estimates:

- **upperAsymptote**: the maximum expected frequency
- **growthRate**: how quickly usage increases
- **lag**: the developmental onset point where growth accelerates

Priors and initial values are provided to stabilize model fitting.


```{r yes_lagModel, include=FALSE}
yes_lagModel <- brm(
  bf(cumulative_ppt  ~ upperAsymptote * exp(-exp(((growthRate*exp(1))/upperAsymptote)*(lag-target_child_age)+1)),
     upperAsymptote ~ 1,
     growthRate ~ 1,
     lag ~ 1,
     nl = TRUE),
  data = filter(functionword_relfreq, logical_word =="si", speaker == "child"),
  
   prior = c(
    prior(uniform(0, 80), nlpar = "upperAsymptote", lb = 0, ub = 80),
     prior(uniform(0, 10), nlpar = "growthRate", lb = 0, ub = 10),
    prior(uniform(10, 72), nlpar = "lag", lb = 10, ub = 72)
  ),

  file = "../modeling/yes_lagModel",

  iter = 10000
)
```

### Estimated Age of Production

This code extracts the estimated lag parameter from the fitted model and stores it in the `age_of_production` dataframe. The lag parameter approximates the developmental onset age for **sí**.

```{r age_of_production_yes}
age_of_production <-
  rbind(age_of_production, c("si", round(fixef(yes_lagModel)[3,],1)))
```


### Prediction Plot

This code visualizes the observed developmental data alongside the fitted Bayesian growth curve for **sí**.

- Black points represent observed child speech data
- The blue line represents the fitted Gompertz growth curve

This allows comparison between the empirical data and the model’s predicted developmental trajectory.

```{r yes_predictions}
yes_predictions <- as.data.frame(fitted(yes_lagModel))

yes_childdata <- filter(functionword_relfreq, logical_word == "si", speaker=="child")
yes_childdata$predictions <- yes_predictions[, "Estimate"]

saveRDS(yes_childdata, "../processed_data/yes_childdata.RDS")
```

this prints out the plot for teh function word si in spanish using all the previous data initialization

```{r Conj_Y_Growth_Model, include=FALSE}
y_lagModel <- brm(
  bf(cumulative_ppt  ~ upperAsymptote * exp(-exp(((growthRate*exp(1))/upperAsymptote)*(lag-target_child_age)+1)),
     upperAsymptote ~ 1,
     growthRate ~ 1,
     lag ~ 1,

  prior = c(

    prior(uniform(0, 72), nlpar = "lag", lb = 0, ub = 72)

  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
iter = 4000,

  ggplot(y_childdata, aes(x = target_child_age, y = cumulative_ppt)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = "Actual Data"), size = 2) + # Original data points
  geom_line(aes(y = predictions, color = "Fitted Values"), size = 1) + # Fitted values
  scale_color_manual(name = "Legend", values = c("Actual Data" = "black", "Fitted Values" = "blue")) +
  theme_bw() + labs(title="Y", x="Child Age (Month)", y="Parts per Thousand") + 
  theme(legend.position = "none") +   
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),

    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14),

  )
## R Markdown

plot(y_plot)
```

# look at the context of or in the childes for spanish to see how its being mapped 
```{r disjunction_o}
functionword_relfreq %>%

  ggplot(aes(target_child_age, cumulative_ppt)) +

```


this allows us to see max amounts to set the priors 
```{r}
functionword_relfreq %>%
  filter(logical_word == "o", speaker == "child") %>%
  summarise(max_ppt = max(cumulative_ppt, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_age = max(target_child_age, na.rm = TRUE))
```

### Bayesian Growth Curve Model

This chunk fits a Bayesian Gompertz growth curve to the developmental trajectory of the Spanish affirmation marker **sí** (“yes”) in child speech.

The model estimates:

- **upperAsymptote**: the maximum expected frequency
- **growthRate**: how quickly usage increases
- **lag**: the developmental onset point where growth accelerates

Priors and initial values are provided to stabilize model fitting.


```{r yes_lagModel, include=FALSE}
o_lagModel <- brm(
  bf(cumulative_ppt  ~ upperAsymptote * exp(-exp(((growthRate*exp(1))/upperAsymptote)*(lag-target_child_age)+1)),
     upperAsymptote ~ 1,
     growthRate ~ 1,
     lag ~ 1,
     nl = TRUE),
  data = filter(functionword_relfreq, logical_word =="si", speaker == "child"),
  

    prior = c(
    prior(uniform(0, 80), nlpar = "upperAsymptote", lb = 0, ub = 80),
    prior(uniform(0, 10), nlpar = "growthRate", lb = 0, ub = 10),
    prior(uniform(0, 72), nlpar = "lag", lb = 0, ub = 72)
  ),
  
  file = "../modeling/o_lagModel",
  iter = 10000
)
```

### Estimated Age of Production

This code extracts the estimated lag parameter from the fitted model and stores it in the `age_of_production` dataframe. The lag parameter approximates the developmental onset age for **sí**.

```{r age_of_production_yes}
age_of_production <-
  rbind(age_of_production, c("o", round(fixef(yes_lagModel)[3,],1)))
```


### Prediction Plot

This code visualizes the observed developmental data alongside the fitted Bayesian growth curve for **sí**.

- Black points represent observed child speech data
- The blue line represents the fitted Gompertz growth curve

This allows comparison between the empirical data and the model’s predicted developmental trajectory.

```{r o_predictions}
o_predictions <- as.data.frame(fitted(o_lagModel))

o_childdata <- filter(functionword_relfreq, logical_word == "o", speaker=="child")
o_childdata$predictions <- o_predictions[, "Estimate"]

saveRDS(o_childdata, "../processed_data/o_childdata.RDS")
```

# saves the split onset files into one file 
```{r save_onset_split}
dir.create("../processed_data", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

saveRDS(filter(age_of_production_no_split, logical_word == "no_sentential"),
        "../processed_data/age_of_production_no_sentential.RDS")

saveRDS(filter(age_of_production_no_split, logical_word == "no_discourse"),
        "../processed_data/age_of_production_no_discourse.RDS")

readRDS("../processed_data/age_of_production_no_sentential.RDS")
readRDS("../processed_data/age_of_production_no_discourse.RDS")
```
